threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can get through a Saturday without pondering which farmer's market has the best sourdough and hipster jam.
Last night on the 43, a bloke serenaded the entire bus with a ukulele. Even the grannies were nodding along. Only in Brockley.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you hear a busker playing techno on the corner while a group of older folks dance in the middle of the street—it's quintessential Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that opens at 3 AM just for the club crowd, serving both drunk revellers and the morning commuters.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know to avoid Dolores Park on sunny weekends—too many tech bros with their speaker setups.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the bus yesterday with a guy practicing his stand-up act. Best part was the punchline about dodging Muni delays—got a round of applause!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plaça, but it's the hidden bars on side streets where the real vibe is. That's where the locals unwind.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their hesitation at the metro turnstiles; only the locals know to push through without thinking.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the Tube app obsessively, while the rest of us just know it’ll be late. Welcome to the life of 'I'll get there when I get there.'
Caught the N137 last night, and a bloke serenaded us with Abba all the way to Clapham. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit casually ordering a currywurst at 3 a.m. after a night out. Just another Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find open-air karaoke on the streets of Kreuzberg; it’s like a spontaneous festival where everyone’s a star, even if they can’t sing.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they know not to trust a bus to be on time, especially with a dog on the tracks or BART falling apart again.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Today, a guy serenaded us on the bus, belting out 'I Will Survive' while a dog in a backpack snoozed. Muni really knows how to keep it quirky.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that Gràcia's plazas aren't just for lounging; they're actually vibrant community hubs where locals catch up with family and friends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look for sidewalks to walk on, instead of just taking over the street like the locals do.
